crossRefs.note: When Moses was done speaking with them, he put a veil on his face.
But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from…
For Christ is the fulfillment of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.
But before faith came, we were kept in custody under the law, confined for the faith which should afterwards be…
So that the law has become our tutor to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
For he is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of separation,
having abolished in his flesh the hostility, the law of commandments contained in ordinances, that he might create in…
which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Christ’s.
For the law, having a shadow of the good to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices…

people.name: Israel
people.line: Patriarch, son of Isaac, father of twelve tribes

people.name: Moses
people.line: Prophet who led Israel out of Egypt

translations.web: and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face, that the children of Israel wouldn’t look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.
translations.bsb: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.
translations.kjv: And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could ➔ not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:
translations.asv: and are not as Moses, who put a veil upon his face, that the children of Israel should not look stedfastly on the end of that which was passing away:
